entities.summary: Eormenric of Kent was a 6th-century king of Kent, ruling from approximately 534/540 to 564/580. He is believed to have succeeded his father Octa of Kent, although the exact relationship is unclear. Eormenric is notable for his role in the Christianization of Kent, which had a lasting impact on the region's history. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that Eormenric's son Æthelberht succeeded him around 580/590. Eormenric's legacy is tied to the conversion of the Kentish king to Christianity, which had far-reaching consequences for the kingdom and its people. The conversion is also linked to the influence of the Catholic Church, which played a significant role in shaping the kingdom's religious landscape. Eormenric's reign marked a turning point in the history of Kent, as it established a Christianized kingdom that would go on to play a significant role in the development of medieval England.
